title: Full cohomological dimension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and put
$$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E,$$
as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $\overline X$ and $Y$ be $S$-schemes whose structure morphisms are of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] commuting with those structure morphisms.

Use the small pro-etale sites and the constant-ring module categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each scheme $T$ write $A_T$ for the constant sheaf of rings with value $A$, $\mathsf M_T=\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$ for its category of module sheaves, and $D_T=D(\mathsf M_T)$ for the derived category. For $\mathcal F\in\mathsf M_T$, write $\iota_T\mathcal F\in D_T$ for the complex with $\mathcal F$ in degree zero and zero in every other degree. Write $\mathcal H_T^r:D_T\to\mathsf M_T$ for the cohomology-sheaf functor [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Only the finite-level total derived direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] are used.

For an integer $c\geq0$, define $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ to be the conjunction of these two clauses:

1. For every $\mathcal F\in\mathsf M_{\overline X}$ and every integer $r>c$,
$$\mathcal H_Y^r\bigl(Rp_*(\iota_{\overline X}\mathcal F)\bigr)=0\quad\text{in }\mathsf M_Y.$$
2. For every object $v:V\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, form the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] $\overline X_V=\overline X\times_YV$, with projections $g_V:\overline X_V\to\overline X$ and $p_V:\overline X_V\to V$ satisfying $p\circ g_V=v\circ p_V$. For every $\mathcal F\in\mathsf M_{\overline X}$ and every integer $r>c$,
$$\mathcal H_V^r\bigl(R(p_V)_*(\iota_{\overline X_V}(g_V^*\mathcal F))\bigr)=0\quad\text{in }\mathsf M_V.$$
Here $g_V^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F|_{\overline X_V}$ is the module-sheaf pullback of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: inverse image followed by extension of scalars from $g_V^{-1}A_{\overline X}$ to $A_{\overline X_V}$. In both clauses $0$ means a zero object of the indicated abelian category, and the coefficient ring is the same $A$. Clause 2 quantifies over sheaves on the original source $\overline X$, then pulls them back. It imposes no constructibility or etale-origin restriction, and no finite-type condition on the site object $V$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$, with the finite-torsion coefficient
convention [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $S$ be a scheme on
which $\ell$ is invertible, let $Y$ and $\overline X$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let $p:\overline X\to
Y$ be a proper $S$-morphism. Use finite-torsion $A$-coefficients and the
derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] $Rp_*$. On the small
pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathcal H^r$
denote the cohomology-sheaf functor
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For an integer $c\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq0}$, write $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ if

$$
 \mathcal H^r(Rp_*\mathcal F)=0\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r>c)
$$

for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $A$-modules on $\overline
X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and, for every object $V\to Y$ of
$Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, if $p_V:\overline X\times_YV\to V$ is the base change
of $p$, then

$$
 \mathcal H^r\bigl(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV})\bigr)=0
 \qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r>c).
$$

*Warning.* Because the quantifier ranges over *every* pro-etale sheaf of
$A$-modules, $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ fails in general, even for $p$
proper and smooth of dimension one over an algebraically closed field: for an
elliptic curve $E$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, $A=\mathbf F_r$ with
$r\neq p$, there is a pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $E$ (not of
etale origin) with $H^n(E_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal F)\neq0$ for every
$n\geq1$. What does hold, with $c=2\dim\overline X$, is the restriction of
the condition to the coefficient sheaves of etale origin.
